domains.name: player
domains.description: Single source of truth for all player identity, profiles, accounts, authentication, preferences, and segmentation across console, PC, and mobile platforms. Owns player registration, parental controls, COPPA/GDPR consent records, player demographics, behavior patterns, engagement metrics (DAU, MAU, WAU, retention), LTV calculations, and player lifecycle management. The authoritative domain for WHO the business serves.

products.name: player_account
products.description: Master identity record and single source of truth for every registered player across all platforms (console, PC, mobile). Stores the canonical player_id, username, display name, avatar, bio, preferred language, locale, timezone, account status (active, suspended, banned, deactivated), account tier, registration timestamp, platform of origin, country of residence, age-verified flag, date of birth, gender identity (self-reported), profile visibility settings, account creation source, and last profile update timestamp. This is the root entity to which all other player domain entities relate via FK. Encompasses both the authentication/identity layer and the player-facing social/demographic profile layer as a single unified entity — industry standard in gaming platforms (PlayFab, AccelByte, GameSparks). Supports GDPR right-to-erasure workflows. Sourced from platform SDK registration flows (Steamworks, PSN, Xbox Live, Nintendo) and Salesforce CRM.

attributes.name: player_account_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the player account. Primary key for the player_account entity. This is the root identity to which all other player domain entities relate.

attributes.name: origin_storefront_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to platform.storefront. Business justification: Player accounts originate on a specific storefront (PSN, Steam, mobile). Platform holder revenue attribution, cross-platform account migration, and acquisition channel reporting require the origin sto

attributes.name: account_level
attributes.description: Player's overall account progression level, earned through gameplay achievements and experience points. Used for matchmaking, content gating, and progression analytics.

attributes.name: account_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the player account. Active accounts have full access; suspended accounts have temporary restrictions; banned accounts are permanently blocked; deactivated accounts are player-initiated closures; pending_verification accounts await email confirmation; locked accounts require password reset.
attributes.references: Platform Terms of Service, Community Standards

attributes.name: account_tier
attributes.description: Subscription or membership tier of the player account. Determines access to premium features, exclusive content, and priority support. Founder tier for early supporters; developer tier for internal testing accounts.

attributes.name: age_verified_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the player's age has been verified through a trusted mechanism (ID verification, credit card validation, or parental consent for minors). Required for access to age-restricted content and features.
attributes.references: COPPA Compliance, ESRB Age Verification, PEGI Age Verification

attributes.name: avatar_url
attributes.description: URL pointing to the player's profile avatar image stored in the CDN (Content Delivery Network). Used for display in social features, leaderboards, and player profiles.

attributes.name: bio
attributes.description: Player-written biography or description displayed on their public profile. Limited to 500 characters. Subject to content moderation policies.

attributes.name: country_code
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code representing the player's country of residence. Used for regional content delivery, compliance with local regulations (GDPR, COPPA, PEGI, ESRB), and geo-specific monetization strategies.
attributes.references: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3, GDPR Territorial Scope, Regional Rating Bodies (ESRB, PEGI, USK, CERO, GRAC)

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: System timestamp when this player_account record was first created in the data warehouse. Used for audit trails and data lineage tracking.
attributes.references: Data Governance Standards, Audit Trail Requirements

attributes.name: creation_source
attributes.description: Marketing attribution source indicating how the player discovered and registered for the game. Used for CPI (Cost Per Install), ROAS (Return on Ad Spend), and marketing campaign effectiveness analysis. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: organic|paid_social|influencer|referral|cross_promotion|app_store|web_direct — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: AppsFlyer Attribution Standards, Adjust Attribution Standards, Marketing Analytics Framework

attributes.name: data_processing_consent_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the player has provided explicit consent for data processing activities beyond essential service delivery (analytics, personalization, third-party sharing). Required for GDPR compliance.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 6, GDPR Article 7 (Conditions for Consent)

attributes.name: data_processing_consent_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the player provided data processing consent. Required for GDPR audit trails demonstrating lawful basis for processing.

attributes.name: date_of_birth
attributes.description: Player's date of birth. Required for age verification, COPPA compliance (children under 13), GDPR consent requirements, and age-gated content access (ESRB, PEGI ratings).
attributes.references: COPPA (Children's Online Privacy Protection Act), GDPR Article 8, ESRB Age Ratings, PEGI Age Ratings

attributes.name: display_name
attributes.description: Public-facing display name shown to other players in-game and in social features. May differ from username and can be changed by the player.

attributes.name: email_address
attributes.description: Primary email address used for account registration, authentication, password recovery, and marketing communications. Must be unique and verified.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 4, COPPA Compliance, CAN-SPAM Act

attributes.name: email_verified_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the player has verified their email address through the verification link sent during registration.

attributes.name: experience_points
attributes.description: Total experience points (XP) accumulated by the player through gameplay activities. Used to calculate account level progression and unlock rewards.

attributes.name: failed_login_attempts
attributes.description: Count of consecutive failed login attempts since the last successful login. Used for account lockout policies and fraud detection. Reset to zero upon successful authentication.
attributes.references: Account Security Standards, Fraud Prevention Framework

attributes.name: gdpr_right_to_erasure_requested_flag
attributes.business_glossary_term: GDPR (General Data Protection Regulation) Right to Erasure Requested Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the player has submitted a GDPR Article 17 Right to Erasure (Right to be Forgotten) request. Triggers data deletion workflows while preserving legally required records.

attributes.name: gender_identity
attributes.description: Self-reported gender identity of the player. Optional field used for demographic analytics and personalized content recommendations. Collected with explicit consent per GDPR and privacy regulations.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 9 (Special Categories), Privacy Best Practices

attributes.name: last_login_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time of the player's most recent successful login. Used for DAU (Daily Active Users), MAU (Monthly Active Users), WAU (Weekly Active Users) calculations, churn prediction, and re-engagement campaigns.
attributes.references: Player Engagement Analytics, Retention Metrics Framework

attributes.name: last_profile_update_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the player last modified their profile information (display name, avatar, bio, or privacy settings). Used for audit trails and profile activity tracking.

attributes.name: locale
attributes.description: Locale identifier combining language and region (e.g., en_US, fr_FR, ja_JP). Used for region-specific formatting of dates, numbers, currency, and culturally appropriate content.

attributes.name: marketing_opt_in_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the player has consented to receive marketing communications (newsletters, promotional offers, game updates). Required for GDPR and CAN-SPAM compliance.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 6 (Lawful Basis for Processing), CAN-SPAM Act, CASL (Canada's Anti-Spam Legislation)

attributes.name: parental_consent_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether verifiable parental consent has been obtained for players under the age of 13 (COPPA) or under 16 (GDPR Article 8). Required for data collection and processing of minors.

attributes.name: password_last_changed_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the player last changed their account password. Used for security audits, password expiration policies, and breach response.

attributes.name: preferred_language
attributes.description: Two-letter ISO 639-1 language code representing the player's preferred language for UI, communications, and in-game content. Used for localization and content delivery.

attributes.name: profile_visibility
attributes.description: Privacy setting controlling who can view the player's profile information. Public profiles are visible to all; friends_only profiles are visible to approved connections; private profiles are visible only to the player.
attributes.references: Privacy Policy, GDPR Article 25 (Privacy by Design)

attributes.name: referral_code
attributes.description: Unique referral code used by the player during registration, linking them to the referring player for viral growth tracking and K-Factor (Viral Coefficient) calculation.
attributes.references: Viral Marketing Framework, Player Acquisition Strategy

attributes.name: registration_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the player account was first created in the system. Used for cohort analysis, retention calculations, and LTV (Lifetime Value) modeling.

attributes.name: reputation_score
attributes.description: Community reputation score based on player behavior, reports, commendations, and moderation actions. Used for matchmaking, trust scoring, and identifying toxic players. Negative scores indicate poor behavior.

attributes.name: suspension_expiry_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when a temporary account suspension will automatically expire and the account will be reactivated. Null for permanent bans.
attributes.references: Moderation Policy, Terms of Service Enforcement

attributes.name: suspension_reason
attributes.description: Detailed reason for account suspension or ban, referencing specific Terms of Service or Community Standards violations. Used for player communication, appeals processing, and moderation analytics.
attributes.references: Terms of Service, Community Standards, Moderation Policy

attributes.name: suspension_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the account was suspended or banned. Used for suspension duration tracking and appeals processing.
attributes.references: Moderation Policy, Terms of Service Enforcement

attributes.name: timezone
attributes.description: IANA timezone identifier (e.g., America/New_York, Europe/London, Asia/Tokyo) representing the player's local timezone. Used for scheduling live events, daily login rewards, and time-based game mechanics.

attributes.name: total_playtime_minutes
attributes.description: Cumulative total playtime across all sessions since account creation, measured in minutes. Used for engagement analysis, LTV (Lifetime Value) modeling, and player segmentation.

attributes.name: two_factor_auth_enabled_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the player has enabled two-factor authentication (2FA) for enhanced account security. Recommended for high-value accounts and required for certain privileged operations.
attributes.references: Account Security Best Practices, PCI DSS Requirement 8.3

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: System timestamp when this player_account record was last modified in the data warehouse. Used for change tracking and incremental ETL (Extract, Transform, Load) processing.
attributes.references: Data Governance Standards, ETL Processing Standards

attributes.name: username
attributes.description: Unique username chosen by the player during registration. Used for login and public identification across platforms. Must be unique system-wide.
attributes.references: Platform SDK Registration Standards (Steamworks, PSN, Xbox Live, Nintendo)

products.name: profile
products.description: Player-facing identity and demographic profile record linked to an account. Stores display name, avatar URL, bio, preferred language, locale, timezone, date of birth, gender identity (self-reported), country, region, profile visibility settings, and last profile update timestamp. Distinct from the account (authentication/identity) — the profile is the social and demographic layer. Supports GDPR right-to-erasure workflows by tracking consent-linked profile fields. Sourced from Salesforce CRM Contact object.

attributes.name: profile_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the player profile. Primary key. Distinct from account_id (authentication layer) — this is the social and demographic identity layer.

attributes.name: player_account_id
attributes.description: Foreign key reference to the player account (authentication/identity layer). Links this profile to the underlying authentication record.

attributes.name: storefront_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to platform.storefront. Business justification: Player profiles have a primary storefront preference driving personalization, storefront-specific content delivery, and platform holder reporting. 'preferred_storefront' and 'platform_preference' are

attributes.name: accessibility_settings
attributes.description: JSON or delimited string capturing player's accessibility preferences (e.g., colorblind mode, subtitle size, controller remapping, audio cues). Used to personalize game experience for players with disabilities.
attributes.references: ADA (Americans with Disabilities Act), WCAG 2.1 (Web Content Accessibility Guidelines)

attributes.name: avatar_url
attributes.description: URL to the player's profile avatar image stored in CDN (Content Delivery Network). Used for visual identity across platforms.

attributes.name: bio
attributes.description: Player-authored biography or profile description. Free-text field subject to content moderation. May be displayed on public profiles.

attributes.name: communication_language
attributes.description: Two-letter ISO 639-1 language code for player support and marketing communications. May differ from preferred_language (UI language). Used for customer service routing and localized campaigns.

attributes.name: content_rating_preference
attributes.description: Player's preferred ESRB (Entertainment Software Rating Board) content rating level for game recommendations and parental controls. Values: E (Everyone), E10 (Everyone 10+), T (Teen), M (Mature 17+), AO (Adults Only 18+).

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the player profile was first created. Used for player tenure analysis, cohort segmentation, and lifecycle tracking. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.

attributes.name: email_verified
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether the player's email address has been verified through a confirmation link or code. Required for account recovery and secure communications.

attributes.name: external_profile_code
attributes.description: Unique identifier from the source system (e.g., Salesforce Contact ID, Steam ID, Epic Account ID). Used for cross-system reconciliation and data lineage tracking.

attributes.name: gdpr_erasure_completed_timestamp
attributes.business_glossary_term: GDPR (General Data Protection Regulation) Erasure Completed Timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when GDPR erasure request was completed and PII (Personally Identifiable Information) was anonymized or deleted. Null if no erasure has been performed. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.

attributes.name: gdpr_erasure_requested
attributes.business_glossary_term: GDPR (General Data Protection Regulation) Erasure Requested
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether the player has requested data erasure under GDPR Article 17 (Right to Erasure). Triggers anonymization workflow and profile soft-deletion.

attributes.name: locale
attributes.description: Locale identifier combining language and region (e.g., en_US, es_MX, fr_FR, de_DE, ja_JP). Used for localization of content, currency, and regional settings.

attributes.name: parental_consent_verified
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether verifiable parental consent has been obtained for players under 13 (COPPA) or under 16 (GDPR Article 8). Required for minors to access online features.
attributes.references: COPPA (Children's Online Privacy Protection Act), GDPR Article 8

attributes.name: phone_verified
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether the player's phone number has been verified through SMS or voice call. Used for two-factor authentication (2FA) and account security.

attributes.name: postal_code
attributes.description: Postal or ZIP code of the player's location. Used for regional analytics, tax compliance, and geo-targeted marketing. May be required for payment processing.
attributes.references: PCI DSS (Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard), GDPR Article 4

attributes.name: preferred_language
attributes.description: Two-letter ISO 639-1 language code representing the player's preferred language for UI (User Interface) and communications (e.g., en, es, fr, de, ja, zh).

attributes.name: profile_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the player profile. Values: active (normal operation), suspended (temporary restriction), banned (permanent restriction), deleted (soft-deleted per GDPR right-to-erasure), pending_verification (awaiting age/identity verification).
attributes.references: Internal Moderation Policy, GDPR Article 17 (Right to Erasure)

attributes.name: referral_code
attributes.description: Unique referral code assigned to this player for viral marketing and K-Factor (Viral Coefficient) tracking. Used when this player refers new players to earn rewards.

attributes.name: referred_by_code
attributes.description: Referral code of the player who referred this player. Used for attribution tracking, referral reward distribution, and viral growth analysis.

attributes.name: region
attributes.description: Sub-national region, state, or province (e.g., California, Ontario, Bavaria). Used for regional analytics, localized events, and compliance with regional regulations.

attributes.name: source_system
attributes.description: Operational system of record that originated this profile record. Values: salesforce_crm (Salesforce CRM Contact object), unity_player_services, epic_games_services, steam, console_sdk, mobile_sdk. Used for data lineage and reconciliation.

attributes.name: timezone
attributes.description: IANA timezone identifier (e.g., America/New_York, Europe/London, Asia/Tokyo). Used for scheduling live events, daily rewards, and time-based features.

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp of the most recent profile update (any field change). Used for tracking profile activity and data freshness. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.

attributes.name: vip_tier
attributes.description: Player's VIP tier based on spending, engagement, or loyalty. Used for tiered rewards, exclusive content access, and premium support. Values: none, bronze, silver, gold, platinum, diamond.

products.name: platform_identity
products.description: Tracks a player's linked external platform identities (PSN ID, Xbox Gamertag, Nintendo Account, Steam ID, Epic Games ID, Apple Game Center, Google Play Games). Each row represents one platform-to-account linkage, storing the external platform type, external platform user ID, platform display name, link status, link timestamp, and last verified timestamp. Enables cross-platform identity resolution and single sign-on federation. Sourced from Steamworks, Console SDKs, and Epic Games Store SDK integrations.

attributes.name: platform_identity_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the platform identity linkage record. Primary key.

attributes.name: device_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to player.device. Business justification: When a player links an external platform identity (PSN, Xbox Gamertag, Nintendo Account, Steam), the linking action is performed from a specific device. Capturing device_id on platform_identity enable

attributes.name: player_account_id
attributes.description: Reference to the internal player account that owns this platform identity linkage. Links to the authoritative player account record in the Player domain.

attributes.name: storefront_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to platform.storefront. Business justification: A platform identity (PSN, Steam, Xbox Live) maps directly to a storefront. Cross-platform play eligibility, platform holder identity verification, and OAuth token management require linking platform i

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this platform identity linkage record was first created in the system. Audit field for data lineage and compliance.

attributes.name: cross_platform_play_enabled_flag
attributes.description: Boolean indicator of whether the player has opted in to cross-platform play (crossplay) using this platform identity. True indicates the player allows matchmaking and interaction with players on other platforms; false indicates platform-exclusive play only.

attributes.name: external_platform_user_code
attributes.description: The unique user identifier assigned by the external platform (e.g., PSN ID, Xbox Gamertag, Steam ID, Epic Account ID). This is the authoritative identifier used by the platform provider to identify the player on their ecosystem.
attributes.references: Platform SDK Documentation (PSN, Xbox Live, Steam, Epic Games Store, Apple Game Center, Google Play Games)

attributes.name: fraud_risk_score
attributes.description: A calculated risk score (0.00 to 100.00) indicating the likelihood that this platform identity linkage is fraudulent or suspicious. Higher scores indicate higher risk. Derived from fraud detection algorithms analyzing linkage patterns, device fingerprints, and platform reputation signals.
attributes.references: Internal Fraud Detection Framework, PCI DSS 3.2.1 Requirement 11.4

attributes.name: last_activity_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when the player last used this platform identity to authenticate or play. Used for identity staleness detection and account security monitoring.

attributes.name: last_verified_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when the platform identity linkage was most recently verified or re-authenticated. Used to track OAuth token refresh cycles and ensure the link remains valid.

attributes.name: link_device_type
attributes.description: The type of device from which the platform identity linkage was performed. Used for device-based analytics and cross-device identity resolution.

attributes.name: link_ip_address
attributes.description: The IP address from which the platform identity linkage request originated. Used for fraud detection, geolocation verification, and security auditing.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 4 (Personal Data Definition), ISO 27001 A.12.4.1 (Event Logging)

attributes.name: link_method
attributes.description: The technical method or flow used to establish the platform identity linkage. OAuth indicates standard OAuth 2.0 authorization flow; sdk_native indicates platform SDK native sign-in; manual_entry indicates player manually entered credentials; platform_sso indicates single sign-on federation; account_merge indicates linkage created during account merge operation.
attributes.references: OAuth 2.0 RFC 6749, Platform SDK Integration Guides

attributes.name: link_source
attributes.description: The application or channel through which the platform identity linkage was initiated. Game_client indicates in-game linking; web_portal indicates account management website; mobile_app indicates companion app; customer_support indicates manual linking by support agent; account_migration indicates bulk migration; platform_auto_link indicates automatic linkage by platform SDK.

attributes.name: link_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the platform identity linkage. Active indicates the link is valid and operational; inactive indicates the player has disconnected the link; suspended indicates temporary restriction; revoked indicates permanent removal; pending_verification indicates awaiting platform OAuth confirmation; expired indicates the OAuth token or link has lapsed.

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for operational notes, customer support annotations, or special handling instructions related to this platform identity linkage. Used for documenting manual interventions, escalations, or account-specific context.

attributes.name: oauth_access_token_hash
attributes.description: One-way cryptographic hash of the OAuth 2.0 access token issued by the platform provider. Stored for audit and token rotation tracking; the actual token is stored in a secure vault. Hash enables token lifecycle management without exposing the credential.

attributes.name: oauth_refresh_token_hash
attributes.description: One-way cryptographic hash of the OAuth 2.0 refresh token issued by the platform provider. Stored for audit and token rotation tracking; the actual token is stored in a secure vault.

attributes.name: platform_account_creation_date
attributes.description: The date when the player originally created their account on the external platform (e.g., when they first registered for PSN, Xbox Live, or Steam). Sourced from platform API profile data where available.

attributes.name: platform_account_tier
attributes.description: The subscription or membership tier of the players account on the external platform (e.g., PlayStation Plus, Xbox Game Pass Ultimate, Nintendo Switch Online). Indicates premium service level and entitlements on the platform.

attributes.name: platform_achievement_count
attributes.description: The total number of achievements, trophies, or gamerscore points the player has earned on the external platform. Sourced from platform achievements API. Used for player engagement and skill segmentation.

attributes.name: platform_age_verified_flag
attributes.description: Boolean indicator of whether the players age has been verified by the external platform provider. True indicates the platform has confirmed the player meets age requirements; false indicates unverified. Critical for COPPA and GDPR compliance.
attributes.references: COPPA 16 CFR Part 312, GDPR Article 8, Platform SDK Documentation

attributes.name: platform_communication_consent_flag
attributes.description: Boolean indicator of whether the player has granted consent for the game publisher to communicate with them via the external platform (e.g., platform notifications, messages). True indicates consent granted; false indicates opt-out.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 6 (Lawful Basis for Processing), CAN-SPAM Act, Platform SDK Messaging Documentation

attributes.name: platform_data_sharing_consent_flag
attributes.description: Boolean indicator of whether the player has granted consent for the game publisher to receive and process their platform profile data (e.g., friends list, achievements, playtime). True indicates consent granted; false indicates opt-out.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 6 (Lawful Basis for Processing), Platform SDK Data Sharing Documentation

attributes.name: platform_display_name
attributes.description: The human-readable display name or gamertag shown on the external platform (e.g., Xbox Gamertag, PSN Online ID, Steam Profile Name). This is the public-facing identity the player uses on that platform.

attributes.name: platform_email_verified_flag
attributes.description: Boolean indicator of whether the players email address has been verified by the external platform provider. True indicates the platform has confirmed email ownership; false indicates unverified. Used for trust scoring and fraud prevention.
attributes.references: Platform API Documentation, OpenID Connect Core 1.0

attributes.name: platform_friend_count
attributes.description: The total number of friends or connections the player has on the external platform. Sourced from platform social graph API. Used for social feature enablement and viral coefficient (K-Factor) analysis.
attributes.references: Platform SDK Social Graph API Documentation

attributes.name: platform_language_code
attributes.description: The two-letter ISO 639-1 language code representing the players preferred language setting on the external platform. Used for localized content delivery and communication.

attributes.name: platform_parental_control_flag
attributes.description: Boolean indicator of whether parental controls are enabled on the players external platform account. True indicates the account is subject to parental restrictions (e.g., content filtering, spending limits, communication restrictions); false indicates no parental controls.
attributes.references: COPPA 16 CFR Part 312, Platform SDK Parental Control Documentation

attributes.name: platform_privacy_level
attributes.description: The privacy setting configured by the player on the external platform for their profile and activity visibility. Public allows all users to view; friends_only restricts to approved connections; private hides from all users.
attributes.references: Platform SDK Privacy Settings Documentation, GDPR Article 25 (Privacy by Design)

attributes.name: platform_region_code
attributes.description: The three-letter ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country or region code associated with the players account on the external platform. Determines regional content availability, pricing, and compliance requirements (e.g., GDPR for EU, COPPA for USA).
attributes.references: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3, Platform SDK Region Documentation

attributes.name: platform_total_playtime_hours
attributes.description: The cumulative total playtime (in hours) the player has logged on the external platform across all games. Sourced from platform activity API where available. Used for player engagement profiling and LTV (Lifetime Value) modeling.

attributes.name: platform_type

products.name: edition_content_inclusion
products.description: This association product represents the bundling relationship between game editions and DLC bundles. It captures which DLC content bundles are included in which edition tiers, with attributes that define how the content is packaged and presented. Each record links one game_edition to one dlc_bundle with inclusion-specific metadata that exists only in the context of this bundling relationship.. Existence Justification: In gaming publishing, edition content bundling is a core commercial product configuration process. Publishers define edition tiers (Standard, Deluxe, Ultimate, Collector's) where each edition includes different combinations of DLC bundles, and the same DLC bundle (e.g., Year 1 Season Pass, Cosmetic Pack) is routinely included across multiple edition tiers with different inclusion terms. Product managers actively configure these bundles, track which content is in which editions, and manage inclusion-specific attributes like display order, inclusion type (pre-order bonus vs. bundled), and price contribution for value proposition analysis.

attributes.name: edition_content_inclusion_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for this edition-DLC inclusion record. Primary key.

attributes.name: dlc_bundle_id
attributes.business_glossary_term: Edition Content Inclusion - Dlc Bundle Id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the DLC bundle included in this edition

attributes.name: game_edition_id
attributes.business_glossary_term: Edition Content Inclusion - Game Edition Id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the game edition that includes this DLC bundle

attributes.name: created_by_user
attributes.description: Username or identifier of the product manager or system user who configured this content inclusion.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this inclusion record was created in the system.

attributes.name: display_order
attributes.description: Numeric sort order for displaying this DLC bundle in the edition's content list on storefronts and marketing materials. Lower numbers appear first.

attributes.name: effective_date
attributes.description: The date when this DLC bundle becomes available to owners of this edition. May differ from edition launch date for timed releases or season pass content.

attributes.name: expiration_date
attributes.description: Optional date when this DLC bundle inclusion expires (for timed exclusives or promotional bundles). Null for permanent inclusions.

attributes.name: included_in_edition
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of game editions (Deluxe, Ultimate, Gold) that include this DLC bundle at no additional cost. Used for bundling and upsell strategies. [Moved from dlc_bundle: This STRING attribute on dlc_bundle is a denormalized representation of the M:N relationship. It stores a comma-separated list of edition names, which is a classic anti-pattern indicating an underlying many-to-many relationship that should be properly modeled in the association table. The association table replaces this denormalized field with proper relational structure.]

attributes.name: inclusion_type
attributes.description: Classification of how this DLC is included in the edition (bundled at launch, pre-order bonus, season pass entitlement, early access window, timed exclusive). Drives entitlement logic and marketing messaging.

attributes.name: is_primary_content
attributes.description: Indicates whether this DLC bundle is a primary selling point for this edition tier (featured in marketing) versus secondary/bonus content.

attributes.name: price_contribution_usd
attributes.description: The estimated value contribution of this DLC bundle to the edition's total MSRP in USD. Used for pricing analysis and value proposition calculations.

products.name: mode_character_roster
products.description: This association product represents the character availability and balance configuration between game modes and playable characters. It captures which characters are permitted in which game modes, with mode-specific balance overrides and unlock requirements. Each record links one game_mode to one playable_character with attributes that exist only in the context of this mode-character pairing.. Existence Justification: In live-service and competitive gaming, character roster management per game mode is a first-class operational entity. A single game mode (e.g., Ranked Competitive) has many playable characters available, and a single character (e.g., a specific hero) is available across many game modes (Campaign, Casual, Ranked, Limited-Time Events). The business actively manages this relationship through balance patches, competitive bans, unlock requirements, and limited-time availability windows.

Supports GaaS live operations cadence and resource allocation.

attributes.name: contract_start_date

attributes.name: gaas_capable

attributes.name: headcount_range

attributes.name: hq_city

attributes.name: hq_state_province

attributes.references: Agiloft/Ironclad IP Clause; IGDA IP Rights Framework

attributes.name: iso27001_certified

attributes.name: pci_dss_compliant

attributes.references: PCI SSC PCI DSS Standard; Apple App Store Review Guidelines; Google Play Developer Program Policies

attributes.name: pegi_registered

attributes.name: qa_embedded
attributes.description: Indicates whether the studio has an embedded Quality Assurance (QA) and playtesting function operating within its production pipeline. True if the studio runs internal QA cycles; False if QA is fully outsourced or handled by the publisher. Drives QA resource allocation and test plan ownership in the quality domain.
attributes.references: Internal QA Governance; IGDA QA Standards

attributes.name: revenue_share_pct
attributes.description: Contractually agreed revenue share percentage payable to the studio from net game revenues. Expressed as a percentage (e.g., 25.00 for 25%). Used for royalty calculation, financial forecasting, and P&L attribution in SAP S/4HANA CO module.
attributes.references: Agiloft/Ironclad Revenue Share Clause; SAP S/4HANA CO

attributes.name: soc2_compliant
attributes.description: Indicates whether the studio has achieved SOC 2 (Service Organization Controls Type 2) compliance for cloud-hosted development infrastructure and services. Used for vendor security risk assessment, particularly for studios operating cloud build pipelines or hosting player-facing services.

attributes.name: specialization
attributes.description: Primary production specialization of the studio indicating the game tier or platform focus. AAA studios produce high-budget console/PC titles; indie studios produce lower-budget creative titles; mobile studios focus on iOS/Android; VR/AR (Virtual Reality/Augmented Reality) studios focus on immersive platforms; casual studios produce mass-market titles; mid-core studios target engaged but non-hardcore audiences; esports studios build competitive titles; engine_tech studios focus on game engine tooling. Drives project assignment eligibility and capability matching. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: aaa|indie|mobile|vr_ar|casual|mid_core|esports|engine_tech — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: IGDA Industry Classification; Internal Studio Capability Registry

attributes.name: studio_code
attributes.description: Short alphanumeric business identifier used to reference the studio in internal systems, Jira project keys, Perforce depot paths, and reporting. Externally known unique code that uniquely identifies the studio across operational systems. Must be uppercase alphanumeric with underscores, 2–20 characters.
attributes.references: Internal Naming Convention; Jira Project Key Standard

attributes.name: studio_name
attributes.description: Official registered or trade name of the game development studio as it appears in corporate directories, contracts, and partner-facing communications. Serves as the primary IDENTITY_LABEL for the studio party. Sourced from corporate directory and contract management system (Agiloft/Ironclad).
attributes.references: Agiloft/Ironclad Contract Management; SAP S/4HANA Vendor Master

attributes.name: studio_status
attributes.description: Current operational lifecycle state of the studio entity. Active studios are engaged in production or live operations; inactive studios have no current projects; on_hold studios are temporarily paused; dissolved studios have ceased operations; acquired studios have been absorbed into the parent organisation; divested studios have been sold or spun off. Drives eligibility for new project assignments and resource allocation.
attributes.references: SAP S/4HANA Vendor Lifecycle; Agiloft/Ironclad Contract Status

attributes.name: studio_type
attributes.description: Classification of the studio's relationship tier with the publishing entity. First-party studios are wholly owned; second-party studios are exclusive partners; third-party studios are independent external developers; co-development studios share production responsibilities; indie studios are self-funded independents; work-for-hire studios deliver contracted deliverables. Drives contractual treatment, revenue sharing, and IP ownership rules. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: first_party|second_party|third_party|co_development|indie|work_for_hire — promote to reference product if additional values are needed]
attributes.references: IGDA Industry Standards; Agiloft/Ironclad Contract Classification

attributes.name: titles_shipped_count
attributes.description: Total number of commercially released game titles shipped by this studio across all platforms and publishing relationships. Used as a proxy for studio experience and production maturity in partner evaluation and project assignment decisions.
attributes.references: Internal Studio Capability Registry; Steamworks/Console SDK Release Records

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the studio master record was most recently modified in the enterprise data platform. Used for change data capture, incremental ETL processing, and audit trail maintenance in the Databricks Lakehouse Silver layer.
attributes.references: Internal Data Governance Audit Standard; ISO/IEC 27001

attributes.name: vcs_depot_path
attributes.description: Root depot path in Perforce Helix Core assigned to this studio for version control and digital asset management. Used to scope code reviews, build triggers, and access control policies. Enables traceability from studio entity to source code and asset repositories.
attributes.references: Perforce Helix Core Version Control; Internal DAM Standards

attributes.name: website_url
attributes.description: Official public website URL for the studio. Used for partner directory listings, due diligence research, and marketing co-promotion materials.

products.name: dev_project
products.description: Master record for each game development project managed within a studio. Tracks project name, associated game title SKU, project type (new IP, sequel, DLC, GaaS live ops update, port), target platforms, development methodology (Agile, Scrum, Kanban), project phase (pre-production, production, alpha, beta, gold master, post-launch), start date, target ship date, and current status. Sourced from Jira project configuration.

attributes.name: dev_project_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for each game development project record in the studio domain. Primary key for the dev_project data product.

Each dev project must be associated with the platform account used for certification submissions, build uploads, and storefront publishing

attributes.name: game_studio_id
attributes.description: Reference to the internal or external development studio responsible for this project. Links to the studio master record.

attributes.name: game_title_id
attributes.description: Reference to the associated game title Stock Keeping Unit (SKU) that this development project is producing or updating. Links to the game title master record.

attributes.name: actual_ship_date
attributes.description: Actual date the game title or update was released to players. Compared against target_ship_date to measure schedule adherence. Populated upon post-launch phase entry.

attributes.name: cert_approval_date
attributes.description: Date on which the platform certification submission was approved by the first-party platform holder. Null until certification is granted. Drives final release scheduling.
attributes.references: Steamworks/Epic Games Store/Console SDKs — Platform Certification; TRC/TCR Standards

attributes.name: cert_submission_date
attributes.description: Date on which the build was submitted to first-party platform holders (e.g., Sony, Microsoft, Nintendo) for Technical Requirements Checklist (TRC) / Technical Certification Requirements (TCR) review via Steamworks or Console SDKs.
attributes.references: Steamworks/Epic Games Store/Console SDKs — Platform Certification; TRC/TCR Standards

attributes.name: cicd_pipeline_url
attributes.description: URL or identifier of the Continuous Integration/Continuous Deployment (CI/CD) build pipeline associated with this project. Used for build automation, release gate management, and deployment tracking.
attributes.references: Internal CI/CD Release Engineering Standards; Perforce Helix Core Build Pipeline Integration

attributes.name: coppa_applicable
attributes.business_glossary_term: Children's Online Privacy Protection Act (COPPA) Applicable Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this project is subject to Children's Online Privacy Protection Act (COPPA) compliance requirements due to targeting players under 13 years of age. Triggers additional data privacy controls and parental consent workflows.
attributes.references: COPPA Enforcement — FTC; GDPR Article 8 (Children's Consent); Apple App Store Review Guidelines; Google Play Developer Program Policies

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this development project record was first created in the system, corresponding to the Jira project creation date/time. Supports audit trail and data lineage requirements.
attributes.references: ISO/IEC 27001 — Information Security Management; SOC 2 — Audit Trail Requirements

attributes.name: critical_bug_count
attributes.description: Current count of critical or blocker severity defect tickets in Jira for this project. A non-zero value typically blocks Gold Master (GM) approval and first-party certification submission.
attributes.references: Jira Project Management — Bug Severity Classification; First-Party TRC/TCR Standards

attributes.name: current_sprint_number
attributes.description: The sequential number of the currently active sprint for this development project as tracked in Jira. Used for progress reporting and velocity analysis.

attributes.name: development_methodology
attributes.description: Software development methodology adopted for this project. Determines sprint cadence, backlog management approach, and release planning structure within Jira.
attributes.references: Jira Project Management — Project Template; IGDA Development Standards

attributes.name: engine_version
attributes.description: Specific version of the game engine in use for this project (e.g., '5.3.2' for Unreal Engine 5.3.2 or '2023.2.1' for Unity). Critical for build pipeline compatibility and Technical Requirements Checklist (TRC) compliance.
attributes.references: Unity Technologies Release Notes; Epic Games Unreal Engine Versioning

attributes.name: game_engine
attributes.description: Primary game engine technology used for development. Determines asset pipeline, rendering, physics, and scripting toolchain. Sourced from project configuration in Unity or Unreal Engine.
attributes.references: Unity Technologies; Epic Games Unreal Engine Documentation

attributes.name: gold_master_date
attributes.description: Date on which the Gold Master (GM) build was approved and locked for manufacturing or digital distribution. Represents the final Quality Assurance (QA) sign-off milestone. Null until the project reaches gold_master phase.
attributes.references: IGDA Game Development Lifecycle; First-Party TRC/TCR Certification Standards

attributes.name: has_mtx
attributes.description: Indicates whether this project includes in-game Microtransactions (MTX) or In-App Purchases (IAP) as part of its monetization model. Triggers additional regulatory review requirements under FTC consumer protection and COPPA compliance for titles targeting minors.
attributes.references: FTC — Consumer Protection and Advertising Standards; COPPA Enforcement; PCI SSC — Payment Processing Standards

attributes.name: has_ugc
attributes.description: Indicates whether this project includes User-Generated Content (UGC) features. Triggers content moderation requirements, GDPR data processing obligations, and compliance review under the European Commission Digital Services Act.
attributes.references: European Commission Digital Services Act; GDPR Supervisory Authorities; FTC Consumer Protection

attributes.name: headcount_allocated
attributes.description: Number of full-time equivalent (FTE) staff allocated to this development project at the current point in time. Used for resource planning and capacity management.
attributes.references: SAP S/4HANA — Human Resources (HR) Module; Internal Resource Allocation Standards

attributes.name: is_first_party
attributes.description: Indicates whether this project is developed by a first-party studio (owned by the console manufacturer or platform holder) as opposed to a third-party external developer/publisher. Affects certification requirements and publishing agreements.
attributes.references: Internal Studio Classification Standards; First-Party/Third-Party Publishing Framework

attributes.name: is_gaas_title
attributes.description: Indicates whether this project is operating under a Game-as-a-Service (GaaS) live operations model with ongoing post-launch content updates and live service management. Drives live ops cadence planning and resource allocation.
attributes.references: Internal GaaS Live Operations Framework; IGDA Live Service Standards

attributes.name: jira_project_key
attributes.description: The unique alphanumeric project key assigned in Jira (e.g., GAME1, DLCX2) that serves as the external business identifier for this development project. Sourced from Jira project configuration and used to cross-reference all sprints, epics, and backlogs.
attributes.references: Jira Project Management — Project Key Convention

attributes.name: milestone_completion_pct
attributes.description: Percentage of project milestones completed relative to total planned milestones, as tracked in Jira. Provides a high-level progress indicator for executive reporting and stakeholder updates.

attributes.name: open_bug_count
attributes.description: Current count of open defect tickets in Jira for this project across all severity levels. Key Quality Assurance (QA) health indicator used in milestone readiness reviews.
attributes.references: Jira Project Management — Bug Tracking; IGDA QA Standards

attributes.name: perforce_depot_path
attributes.description: Root depot path in Perforce Helix Core version control system for this project's digital assets and source code (e.g., '//depot/games/project-titan/main'). Used for build pipeline integration and digital asset management.
attributes.references: Perforce Helix Core — Version Control and Digital Asset Management

attributes.name: project_code
attributes.description: Internal alphanumeric code used for budget tracking, SAP S/4HANA cost center allocation, and cross-system referencing of this development project.

attributes.name: project_description
attributes.description: Free-text description of the development project scope, objectives, and key deliverables as documented in Jira project configuration. Used for stakeholder communication and project onboarding.

attributes.name: project_name
attributes.description: Human-readable name of the game development project as configured in Jira (e.g., 'Project Titan — Season 3 Live Ops Update'). Used in reporting, dashboards, and stakeholder communications.

attributes.name: project_phase
attributes.description: Current phase in the game development lifecycle. Values: pre_production, production, alpha, beta, gold_master (Gold Master (GM) — final build approved for manufacturing/distribution), post_launch. Sourced from Jira project status and milestone tracking.
attributes.references: IGDA Game Development Lifecycle Standards; Jira Milestone Configuration

attributes.name: project_status
attributes.description: Current operational lifecycle status of the development project. Distinct from project_phase (which tracks development stage); this field tracks the administrative state of the project record.

attributes.name: project_type
attributes.description: Classification of the development project by its production scope. Values: new_ip (original Intellectual Property (IP)), sequel (follow-up to existing title), dlc (Downloadable Content (DLC) expansion), gaas_live_ops (Game-as-a-Service (GaaS) live operations update), port (platform port), remaster (remastered edition).
attributes.references: Internal Game Development Taxonomy; IGDA Project Classification Standards

attributes.name: soft_launch_date
attributes.description: Date of the soft launch — a limited regional or audience release used to validate live operations, monetization, and stability before the full hard launch. Applicable primarily to mobile and GaaS titles.
attributes.references: Internal Launch Management Framework; AppsFlyer/Adjust — Mobile Attribution

attributes.name: sprint_cadence_weeks
attributes.description: Duration of each sprint in weeks as configured in Jira for Scrum or Agile projects (typically 1, 2, or 3 weeks). Drives sprint planning, backlog grooming, and velocity tracking.

attributes.name: start_date
attributes.description: Official start date of the development project, marking the beginning of active production work. Corresponds to the project start date configured in Jira.

attributes.name: target_platforms
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of target distribution platforms for this project (e.g., 'PS5,Xbox Series X,PC,Switch,iOS,Android'). Drives platform certification (Technical Requirements Checklist (TRC) / Technical Certification Requirements (TCR)) planning and Steamworks/Console SDK integration scope. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: ps5|xbox_series_x|xbox_series_s|pc|switch|ios|android|ps4|xbox_one|vr — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: Steamworks/Epic Games Store/Console SDKs — Platform Certification; TRC/TCR Requirements

attributes.name: target_ship_date
attributes.description: Planned release or ship date for the game title or update produced by this project. Used for milestone planning, first-party certification scheduling, and marketing campaign alignment.
attributes.references: Jira Project Management — Release Planning; Steamworks/Console SDK Certification Timelines

attributes.name: uat_sign_off_date
attributes.description: Date on which User Acceptance Testing (UAT) was formally signed off by the designated approver, confirming the build meets acceptance criteria prior to first-party certification submission.
attributes.references: IGDA QA and UAT Standards; First-Party TRC/TCR Certification Requirements

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp of the most recent update to this development project record. Used for change tracking, incremental data pipeline processing, and audit compliance.
attributes.references: ISO/IEC 27001 — Information Security Management; SOC 2 — Audit Trail Requirements

products.name: sprint
products.description: Jira-sourced sprint records for each development project. Captures sprint name, sprint number, sprint goal, start date, end date, velocity (story points committed vs. completed), sprint state (active, closed, future), and associated board. Enables sprint-over-sprint velocity tracking and GaaS live ops cadence management.

attributes.name: sprint_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for each sprint record in the Databricks Silver Layer. Primary key for the sprint data product sourced from Jira sprint management.

attributes.name: dev_project_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the game development project associated with this sprint. Links the sprint to the broader production pipeline and game title context.

attributes.name: game_studio_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the internal or external development studio responsible for executing this sprint. Supports multi-studio production tracking and resource allocation reporting.

attributes.name: milestone_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the production milestone (e.g., Alpha, Beta, Gold Master, Launch) to which this sprint contributes. Enables milestone-level aggregation of sprint velocity and delivery progress.
attributes.references: Gaming Studio Domain Model; Jira Software

attributes.name: regulatory_obligation_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.regulatory_obligation. Compliance dashboards need to

attributes.name: added_story_points
attributes.description: Story points added to the sprint scope after sprint planning commenced (scope creep). Tracks mid-sprint additions that affect velocity accuracy and predictability.

attributes.name: blockers_count
attributes.description: Number of active impediments or blockers logged against this sprint in Jira. High blocker counts are a leading indicator of sprint failure and are tracked for escalation and retrospective analysis.
attributes.references: Jira Software REST API v3; Scrum Guide 2020

attributes.name: board_reference
attributes.description: Identifier of the Jira Scrum board to which this sprint belongs. A board typically maps to a single game development project or studio team.

attributes.name: bug_issues
attributes.description: Number of Jira issues classified as bugs within the sprint. Tracks QA debt and defect injection rate, which is critical for game quality assurance and release gate readiness.
attributes.references: Jira Software REST API v3; IGDA Quality Standards

attributes.name: build_number
attributes.description: Internal build identifier generated by the CI/CD pipeline for the sprint's primary deliverable build. Used to correlate sprint output with QA test executions and release gate assessments.

attributes.name: committed_story_points
attributes.description: Total story points committed to the sprint at sprint planning. Represents the team's planned velocity and capacity for the sprint. Core input for velocity tracking and capacity planning.
attributes.references: Jira Software REST API v3; Scrum Guide 2020

attributes.name: completed_date
attributes.description: Actual date the sprint was closed or completed in Jira. May differ from end_date when sprints are extended or closed early. Null for active or future sprints.

attributes.name: completed_issues
attributes.description: Number of Jira issues resolved or closed within the sprint. Used alongside completed_story_points to assess sprint throughput and team delivery rate.

attributes.name: completed_story_points
attributes.description: Total story points for issues marked as 'Done' by the end of the sprint. Represents actual velocity delivered. Used for sprint-over-sprint velocity trending and team performance analysis.
attributes.references: Jira Software REST API v3; Scrum Guide 2020

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the sprint record was first created in the source system (Jira). Represents the business event time of sprint creation, used for audit trail and data lineage in the Silver Layer.
attributes.references: Jira Software REST API v3; ISO/IEC 27001

attributes.name: duration_days
attributes.description: Planned duration of the sprint in calendar days, derived from the difference between start_date and end_date at sprint creation. Standard sprint durations in game development are typically 7, 14, or 21 days.

attributes.name: end_date
attributes.description: Planned or actual end date of the sprint (yyyy-MM-dd). Used to determine sprint duration, identify overruns, and align with milestone and release gate schedules.

attributes.name: epic_key
attributes.description: Identifier of the primary Jira Epic associated with this sprint. Supports epic-level rollup of sprint delivery and feature progress tracking across the production backlog.

attributes.name: goal

attributes.references: Scrum Guide 2020; Jira Software REST API v3

attributes.name: health
attributes.description: Qualitative health indicator for the sprint as assessed by the Scrum Master or project manager. 'on_track' indicates delivery is proceeding as planned; 'at_risk' indicates potential blockers; 'off_track' indicates significant impediments to goal achievement.

attributes.name: incomplete_issues
attributes.description: Number of Jira issues not completed by sprint end. Carried-over issues impact the next sprint's planning and are a key indicator of sprint health and scope management.

attributes.name: is_gaas_sprint
attributes.business_glossary_term: Game as a Service (GaaS) Sprint Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this sprint is part of a live operations (GaaS) cadence rather than a pre-launch development cycle. Enables segmentation of live-ops velocity from core development velocity in analytics.

attributes.name: jira_sprint_key
attributes.description: Native sprint identifier assigned by Jira. Used to trace the record back to the operational source system (Jira Software) for reconciliation and lineage purposes.

attributes.name: perforce_changelist

attributes.name: qa_sign_off

attributes.name: release_gate_status

attributes.name: release_version
attributes.description: Semantic version number of the game build or patch targeted by this sprint (e.g., '1.4.2', '2.0.0.1'). Aligns sprint work with the release pipeline and CI/CD deployment gates.

attributes.name: removed_story_points
attributes.description: Story points removed from the sprint scope after sprint planning commenced. Tracks descoping decisions that affect velocity accuracy and sprint health.

attributes.name: retrospective_notes
attributes.description: Free-text summary of key findings, action items, and process improvement decisions captured during the sprint retrospective. Supports continuous improvement tracking and GaaS cadence optimization.

attributes.name: source_system
attributes.description: Identifies the originating operational system for this sprint record. Primarily 'jira' for Jira Software-sourced records; 'manual' for records entered directly; 'import' for bulk-loaded historical data.

attributes.name: sprint_name
attributes.description: Human-readable name of the sprint as defined in Jira (e.g., 'Alpha-Sprint-14', 'LiveOps-Week-22'). Used for display in dashboards, velocity reports, and GaaS cadence tracking.

attributes.name: sprint_number
attributes.description: Sequential ordinal number of the sprint within its project or board. Enables sprint-over-sprint velocity trending and milestone progression analysis.

attributes.name: sprint_state
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the sprint as reported by Jira. 'active' indicates the sprint is in progress; 'closed' indicates it has been completed; 'future' indicates it is planned but not yet started.

attributes.name: sprint_type
attributes.description: Classification of the sprint by its primary purpose within the game development lifecycle. 'development' covers feature work; 'live_ops' covers GaaS live operations cadence; 'qa' covers Quality Assurance cycles; 'hardening' covers stability and bug-fix sprints; 'release' covers gold master and launch preparation; 'spike' covers research or proof-of-concept work.

attributes.name: start_date
attributes.description: Planned or actual start date of the sprint (yyyy-MM-dd). Used for timeline planning, capacity scheduling, and sprint cadence reporting.

attributes.name: team_capacity_points
attributes.description: Total story point capacity available to the team for this sprint, accounting for planned absences, holidays, and part-time allocations. Used to assess commitment accuracy and identify over- or under-commitment patterns.
attributes.references: Scrum Guide 2020; Gaming Studio Capacity Planning

attributes.name: team_size
attributes.description: Number of active team members participating in this sprint. Supports per-capita velocity normalization and resource allocation analysis across studios.

attributes.name: total_issues
attributes.description: Total number of Jira issues (stories, tasks, bugs, sub-tasks) included in the sprint at any point. Provides a count-based complement to story-point-based velocity metrics.

attributes.name: uat_sign_off
attributes.description: Indicates whether User Acceptance Testing (UAT) has been completed and signed off for this sprint's deliverables. Required for release gate approval and production deployment authorization.
attributes.references: Gaming Studio UAT Process; Jira Software

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp of the most recent modification to the sprint record in the source system (Jira). Used for incremental ETL processing, change detection, and audit compliance in the Databricks Silver Layer.
attributes.references: Jira Software REST API v3; ISO/IEC 27001
