attributes.name: bracket_name
attributes.description: Human-readable name or label for the bracket stage, such as 'Upper Bracket', 'Lower Bracket', 'Group A', 'Playoffs', 'Qualifier Round 1'. Used for display and reporting purposes.

attributes.name: bracket_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the bracket. Draft indicates planning phase; scheduled means bracket is finalized and awaiting start; in_progress indicates active matches; completed means all matches finished; cancelled means bracket was terminated; suspended indicates temporary halt.

attributes.name: bracket_type
attributes.description: The competitive format structure of the bracket. Single elimination removes teams after one loss; double elimination allows one loss before elimination; round robin has all teams play each other; Swiss pairs teams with similar records; GSL group is a dual-tournament group stage; page playoff is a four-team format; gauntlet is a sequential challenge format. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: single_elimination|double_elimination|round_robin|swiss|gsl_group|page_playoff|gauntlet — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: broadcast_language_codes
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of ISO 639-1 two-letter language codes for broadcast coverage of this bracket. Example: 'en,es,pt,zh,ko,ja'. Used for localization planning and international audience tracking.

attributes.name: broadcast_priority
attributes.description: The broadcast coverage priority level for matches within this bracket. Primary indicates main stream coverage; secondary indicates alternate stream; tertiary indicates limited or VOD-only coverage; none indicates no broadcast planned.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this bracket record was first created in the system. Used for audit trail and data lineage tracking.

attributes.name: end_date
attributes.description: The scheduled or actual date when the final match of this bracket stage is planned to complete or did complete. Used for tournament duration tracking and venue booking.

attributes.name: game_version
attributes.description: The specific patch, build, or version number of the game title used for this bracket stage. Critical for competitive integrity as balance changes between versions can affect gameplay. Example: '13.4', 'Season 7 Patch 2', 'Build 2023.11.15'.

attributes.name: grand_final_reset_flag
attributes.description: For double elimination brackets, indicates whether the grand final requires a bracket reset if the upper bracket finalist loses. True means the lower bracket winner must win two series; false means single series determines champion regardless of bracket path.

attributes.name: match_scheduling_buffer_minutes
attributes.description: The standard time buffer in minutes allocated between consecutive matches in this bracket for player breaks, technical setup, and broadcast transitions. Used for automated scheduling and production planning.

attributes.name: modified_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this bracket record was last updated. Used for change tracking and data synchronization across systems.

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for tournament organizers to capture operational notes, special circumstances, rule exceptions, or other contextual information about this bracket stage. Used for internal communication and historical reference.

attributes.name: peak_ccu
attributes.description: The maximum number of concurrent viewers across all broadcast channels during this bracket stage. Key performance indicator for broadcast success and sponsorship value. Measured across Twitch, YouTube, in-game spectator, and other platforms.

attributes.name: prize_pool_allocation_pct
attributes.description: The percentage of the total tournament prize pool allocated to this specific bracket stage. For example, if the main event bracket receives 80% of the total prize pool, this value would be 80.00. Used for prize distribution calculations and financial reporting.

attributes.name: region
attributes.description: The geographic region this bracket represents or is restricted to. NAM is North America; EUR is Europe; ASA is Asia-Pacific; CHN is China; KOR is South Korea; JPN is Japan; LAT is Latin America; OCE is Oceania; MEA is Middle East and Africa; GLOBAL indicates multi-region or international bracket. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: NAM|EUR|ASA|CHN|KOR|JPN|LAT|OCE|MEA|GLOBAL — 10 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: replay_review_enabled_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether match officials can review replays for disputed calls or rule violations during matches in this bracket. True means replay review is available; false means real-time officiating only.

attributes.name: round_count
attributes.description: Total number of competitive rounds within this bracket stage. For single elimination with 8 teams this would be 3 (quarterfinals, semifinals, finals). For round robin this represents the number of match days or cycles.

attributes.name: ruleset_version
attributes.description: The version identifier of the competitive ruleset document governing this bracket. Tracks which set of tournament rules, map pools, character restrictions, and competitive settings apply. Example: 'LCS 2024 Spring v1.2', 'TI12 Official Rules v3.0'.

attributes.name: seeding_method
attributes.description: The methodology used to determine initial team placement and matchup order within the bracket. Manual indicates tournament organizer assignment; performance-based uses historical stats; random draw is lottery-based; regional ranking uses geographic league standings; points-based uses accumulated tournament points; previous stage uses results from prior bracket.

attributes.name: spectator_mode
attributes.description: The audience access model for this bracket stage. Live audience indicates in-person attendance allowed; online only means digital viewing only; hybrid allows both in-person and online; closed means no public viewing (internal/qualifier matches).

attributes.name: sponsor_tier
attributes.description: The highest sponsorship tier associated with this bracket stage. Title sponsor has naming rights; presenting sponsor has secondary branding; official sponsor has category exclusivity; supporting sponsor has standard placement; none indicates no dedicated bracket sponsorship.

attributes.name: start_date
attributes.description: The scheduled date when the first match of this bracket stage is planned to begin. Used for tournament scheduling, broadcast planning, and player availability coordination.

attributes.name: team_count
attributes.description: Number of teams or competitors participating in this bracket stage. Used for bracket structure validation and seeding calculations.

attributes.name: technical_pause_allowed_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether teams are permitted to request technical pauses during matches in this bracket. True means pauses are allowed per ruleset; false means no pauses permitted (typically for lower-tier or online qualifiers).

attributes.name: third_place_match_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this bracket includes a third-place playoff match between the two semifinal losers. True means a bronze medal match is scheduled; false means no third-place match.

attributes.name: tiebreaker_rule
attributes.description: Business rule defining how ties in standings or match results are resolved. Examples: 'Head-to-head record', 'Map differential', 'Total kills', 'Sudden death overtime', 'Coin flip'. Free-text field capturing the specific tiebreaker logic for this bracket.

attributes.name: total_viewership
attributes.description: The cumulative number of unique viewers who watched any portion of this bracket stage across all broadcast channels. Used for sponsorship reporting and media rights valuation.

products.name: match
products.description: Core transactional record for competitive matches encompassing the full match lifecycle from scheduling through post-match analytics. At match header level: date/time, tournament/bracket round, best-of format (BO1/BO3/BO5), venue type (online/LAN), patch version, referee/admin assignment, CCU metrics, match status, and winner determination. At game/map detail level: game number within the series, map/mode played, per-game scores, winning team, duration in seconds, game start/end timestamps, server region, and disqualification flags. At player performance detail level: per-player-per-game KDA (kills/deaths/assists), damage dealt, healing done, objective score, economy score, MVP flag, role-specific KPIs (CS/min for MOBA, headshot rate for FPS, APM for RTS), and game-title-specific stat fields. This is the single source of truth for all competitive match data from header through game results through player statistics.

attributes.name: exclusivity_scope
attributes.description: Detailed description of the exclusivity terms, including any carve-outs, co-exclusive arrangements, or platform-specific restrictions (e.g., exclusive for streaming but non-exclusive for linear TV).

attributes.name: highlights_rights_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the agreement includes rights to create and distribute highlight clips and short-form content. True if highlights rights are granted; False otherwise.

attributes.name: language_requirements
attributes.description: Languages in which the broadcast must be available, including commentary, subtitles, and localization requirements. May specify primary and secondary languages (e.g., English primary, Spanish and Portuguese secondary).

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this broadcast rights record was last updated. Used for audit trail and change tracking.

attributes.name: license_fee_amount
attributes.description: Total license fee paid by the rights holder for the broadcast rights over the term of the agreement. Represents the guaranteed minimum payment.

attributes.name: license_fee_currency
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for the license fee amount (e.g., USD, EUR, GBP, JPY).

attributes.name: live_broadcast_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the agreement includes rights to broadcast live matches and events. True if live broadcasting is permitted; False if only delayed or on-demand content is allowed.

attributes.name: localization_requirements
attributes.description: Detailed localization requirements beyond language, including cultural adaptations, regional commentary talent, local sponsorship integration, and territory-specific content adjustments.

attributes.name: minimum_guaranteed_viewership
attributes.description: Minimum number of concurrent or cumulative viewers that the rights holder guarantees to deliver as part of the Service Level Agreement (SLA). Nullable if no viewership guarantee exists.

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-form notes and additional context about the broadcast rights agreement, including special provisions, historical context, or operational considerations not captured in structured fields.

attributes.name: performance_bonus_structure
attributes.description: Structure of performance-based bonuses payable to the league or tournament organizer based on viewership milestones, engagement metrics, or other KPIs. Nullable if no performance bonuses exist.

attributes.name: platform_type
attributes.description: Type of broadcast platform covered by the agreement. Streaming includes OTT and digital platforms; linear TV includes traditional broadcast and cable; in-game spectator refers to native game client viewing.

attributes.name: production_quality_standards
attributes.description: Minimum production quality standards required by the agreement, including resolution (e.g., 1080p, 4K), frame rate (e.g., 60 FPS), audio quality, and technical specifications.

attributes.name: production_responsibility
attributes.description: Party responsible for producing the broadcast, including camera work, commentary, graphics, and technical production. May be the rights holder, the league/tournament organizer, a shared arrangement, or a contracted third party.

attributes.name: renewal_option_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the agreement includes an option for the rights holder to renew the broadcast rights for an additional term. True if renewal option exists; False otherwise.

attributes.name: renewal_terms
attributes.description: Terms and conditions governing the renewal option, including renewal period duration, pricing adjustments, notice period required, and any changes to rights scope or exclusivity.

attributes.name: revenue_share_basis
attributes.description: Defines the basis on which revenue share is calculated: gross revenue, net revenue after costs, advertising revenue only, subscription revenue only, or not applicable if no revenue share exists.

attributes.name: revenue_share_percentage
attributes.description: Percentage of advertising, subscription, or other broadcast-related revenue that the rights holder must share with the league or tournament organizer. Nullable if the agreement is a flat-fee arrangement with no revenue share.

attributes.name: rights_end_date
attributes.description: Date when the broadcast rights agreement expires. Nullable for open-ended or perpetual agreements subject to termination clauses.

attributes.name: rights_holder_name
attributes.description: Name of the organization or entity that holds the broadcast rights (e.g., Twitch, YouTube Gaming, ESPN, NBC Sports).

attributes.name: rights_holder_type
attributes.description: Classification of the rights holder by platform type. Distinguishes between streaming platforms, traditional television, in-game spectator modes, and other distribution channels. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: streaming_platform|linear_tv|cable_network|digital_network|in_game_spectator|social_media|other — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: rights_start_date
attributes.description: Date when the broadcast rights agreement becomes effective and the rights holder may begin broadcasting.

attributes.name: signed_date
attributes.description: Date when the broadcast rights agreement was signed by all parties. Represents the legal execution date of the contract.

attributes.name: sponsorship_integration_rights
attributes.description: Rights and restrictions regarding integration of the rights holder's own sponsors into the broadcast, including on-screen branding, sponsored segments, and product placement. May include conflict-of-interest clauses with league sponsors.

attributes.name: sublicensing_allowed_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the rights holder is permitted to sublicense the broadcast rights to third parties. True if sublicensing is allowed; False if the rights are non-transferable.

attributes.name: sublicensing_terms
attributes.description: Detailed terms and conditions governing sublicensing, including approval requirements, revenue share on sublicensed deals, and restrictions on sublicensee types or territories.

attributes.name: termination_clause
attributes.description: Summary of termination conditions and notice requirements, including breach conditions, force majeure provisions, and early termination penalties or buyout terms.

attributes.name: viewership_metric_type
attributes.description: Type of viewership metric used for the minimum guaranteed viewership SLA. CCU (Concurrent Users), PCU (Peak Concurrent Users), total views, unique viewers, or watch hours.

attributes.name: vod_rights_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the agreement includes rights to offer video-on-demand replays and archived content. True if VOD rights are granted; False if only live or time-limited content is permitted.

domains.name: content
domains.description: Owns the digital asset pipeline for all in-game content: art assets, audio, localization strings, level/map data, NPC definitions, textures, and UGC moderation queues. Manages LOD asset variants, content versioning in Perforce Helix Core, live-ops content drops (seasonal events, patches, hotfixes), and asset lifecycle from creation to deployment. Distinct from title: title owns the product catalog; content owns the asset and creative deliverable layer.

products.name: asset
products.description: Master record for every digital asset in the game content pipeline — art, audio, texture, mesh, animation, shader, VFX, UI element, video, and scripted data. Tracks asset name, type, format, file size, resolution/bitrate specs, LOD tier, platform target, engine compatibility (Unity/Unreal), creation date, author, current lifecycle status (draft, review, approved, deprecated), Perforce depot path, content hash for integrity verification, classification tags (genre, art style, feature area, platform, sensitivity), audio-specific metadata (sample rate, bit depth, channel config, middleware format like Wwise/FMOD), supported locale list, and locale-specific variant flags. This is the authoritative SSOT for all creative deliverables managed in Perforce Helix Core, including locale reference data for asset-level localization targeting.
products.reference: Digital Asset Management (DAM) — Perforce Helix Core Asset Record

products.name: content_release
products.description: Unified live-ops content release record representing any scheduled or emergency delivery of new or updated content to live players. Covers all release types via type discrimination: seasonal events (with event theme, start/end timestamps, recurrence pattern, featured bundles, exclusive rewards, participation mechanics, eligibility rules), patches and hotfixes (with semver version string, patch type, mandatory flag, minimum client version, per-platform size, QA sign-off, gold master date, TRC/TCR certification status), battle pass seasons, DLC drops, and limited-time events. Also serves as the release calendar, capturing planned vs actual release dates, release window (soft/hard), marketing campaign alignment, and cross-functional approval status. Stores drop name, release type, scheduled go-live timestamp, actual go-live timestamp, rollback timestamp, target platforms, associated asset bundles, release notes reference, live-ops owner, and deployment status. The single operational heartbeat of GaaS content delivery — one entity to answer 'what is going live, when, and what does it contain'.

products.name: bundle_manifest_entry
products.description: This association product represents the inclusion of a specific asset within an asset bundle's manifest. It captures the operational reality of game content packaging where assets are explicitly assigned to bundles with specific ordering, roles, and LOD configurations. Each record links one asset_bundle to one asset with metadata that exists only in the context of this packaging relationship.. Existence Justification: In game development, bundle manifests are operational artifacts that content engineers actively create, version, and manage. A single asset (e.g., a character texture) is routinely packaged into multiple bundles (base game, DLC, platform-specific builds, patch bundles) with different compression settings, LOD tiers, and load priorities. Conversely, each bundle contains hundreds to thousands of assets with explicit ordering and role assignments. This is a core content pipeline operation, not an analytical correlation.

The COUNT of manifest entries provides the true asset count.]

products.name: npc_spawn_configuration
products.description: This association product represents the spawn configuration between level_map and npc_definition. It captures the authoritative encounter design decisions made by level designers specifying which NPC archetypes appear in which levels, under what conditions, and with what spawn parameters. Each record links one level_map to one npc_definition with spawn-specific attributes that exist only in the context of this level-NPC pairing.. Existence Justification: In game development, level designers actively manage encounter design by configuring which NPC archetypes spawn in which levels. A single level contains multiple different NPC types (enemies, vendors, quest givers), and a single NPC archetype definition is reused across multiple levels with level-specific spawn parameters. This is a recognized operational business process called encounter design or spawn configuration management.

attributes.description: Number of players who have added this UGC submission to their favorites or wishlist. Indicates sustained player interest beyond initial download and is used for community engagement analytics and recommendation ranking.
attributes.references: Gaming Internal Data Standards; GameAnalytics/Amplitude Player Behavior Analytics

attributes.name: file_size_bytes
attributes.description: Total file size of the UGC asset package in bytes. Used for CDN storage capacity planning, download time estimation, platform certification size limit checks, and player-facing display. Serves as the principal MEASUREMENT_OR_VALUE for this MASTER_RESOURCE.
attributes.references: Gaming Internal Data Standards; Steamworks SDK; Apple App Store Review Guidelines; Google Play Developer Program Policies

attributes.name: game_engine_version
attributes.description: Version of the game engine (Unity or Unreal Engine) used to create or required to run this UGC submission. Critical for compatibility validation during the asset pipeline ingestion and platform certification process.
attributes.references: Unity Engine Documentation; Unreal Engine Documentation; Gaming Internal Data Standards

attributes.name: ip_clearance_status
attributes.description: Status of intellectual property rights clearance review for this UGC submission. Ensures the content does not infringe on third-party IP, trademarks, or copyrights before approval and distribution.
attributes.references: FTC Consumer Protection Standards; European Commission Digital Services Act; IGDA IP Guidelines; Gaming Internal Data Standards

attributes.name: is_age_restricted
attributes.description: Indicates whether this UGC submission requires age verification before access, based on content rating classification. Enforces COPPA compliance for underage players and platform age-gating requirements.
attributes.references: COPPA (Children's Online Privacy Protection Act); ESRB; PEGI; Apple App Store Review Guidelines; Google Play Developer Program Policies

attributes.name: is_cross_platform_compatible
attributes.description: Indicates whether this UGC submission is certified as compatible across multiple gaming platforms (PC, console, mobile). Drives cross-platform distribution eligibility and platform certification routing.
attributes.references: Console Platform TRC/TCR Standards; Steamworks SDK; Gaming Internal Data Standards

attributes.name: is_featured
attributes.description: Indicates whether this UGC submission has been editorially selected as featured content by the community management team. Featured content receives prominent placement in workshop listings and community portals.

attributes.name: is_monetization_eligible
attributes.description: Indicates whether this UGC submission is eligible for in-game monetization programs (e.g., creator marketplace, revenue share, MTX integration). Determined by content type, approval status, and creator agreement acceptance.
attributes.references: Gaming Internal Data Standards; FTC Advertising Standards; GDPR Article 6

attributes.name: language_code
attributes.description: ISO 639-1 language code (optionally with ISO 3166-1 region subtag) indicating the primary language of the UGC submission's text content (e.g., 'en', 'fr', 'de', 'ja'). Used for localization filtering and regional content compliance.
attributes.references: ISO 639-1 Language Codes; ISO 3166-1 Country Codes; GDPR Article 12 (language accessibility)

attributes.name: last_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp of the most recent update to the UGC submission record, including creator-initiated version updates, moderation status changes, or metadata edits. Supports audit trail and change detection in the Silver layer.
attributes.references: Gaming Internal Data Standards; ISO 8601; ISO/IEC 27001

attributes.name: license_type
attributes.description: Licensing terms under which the UGC submission is distributed. Governs redistribution rights, modification permissions, and commercial use eligibility for the creator's content.
attributes.references: Creative Commons License Standards; Gaming Internal Data Standards; IGDA IP Guidelines

attributes.name: nps_score
attributes.description: Net Promoter Score collected from players who interacted with this UGC submission, on a scale of -100 to 100. Measures player satisfaction and likelihood to recommend the content. Feeds community health KPI dashboards in Tableau/Looker.
attributes.references: NPS Methodology (Bain & Company); Gaming Internal Data Standards; GameAnalytics/Amplitude

attributes.name: platform_target
attributes.description: The gaming platform(s) for which this UGC submission is designed and compatible. Drives platform-specific certification checks, distribution routing, and compatibility filtering in workshop listings.
attributes.references: Steamworks SDK; Epic Games Store SDK; Console Platform TRC/TCR Standards; Gaming Internal Data Standards

attributes.name: preview_image_url
attributes.description: Secure HTTPS URL for the thumbnail or preview image of the UGC submission displayed in community portals, workshop listings, and in-game browsing interfaces. Supports player discovery and click-through engagement.
attributes.references: Gaming Internal Data Standards; Steamworks SDK

attributes.name: price_virtual_currency
attributes.description: Price of the UGC submission in the game's virtual currency units (e.g., coins, gems, credits) if sold through the in-game marketplace. Zero or null indicates free content. Supports in-game monetization (MTX/IAP) analytics.
attributes.references: Gaming Internal Data Standards; PCI SSC (Payment Card Industry Security Standards Council); SAP S/4HANA FI Module

attributes.name: published_date
attributes.description: Calendar date when the UGC submission was first made publicly available to the player community. Used for date-based reporting, anniversary promotions, and community content calendars.

attributes.name: rating_count
attributes.description: Total number of individual player ratings submitted for this UGC asset. Used alongside rating_score to assess statistical confidence of the aggregate rating and prevent manipulation by low-volume outliers.

attributes.name: rating_score
attributes.description: Aggregate community rating score for the UGC submission, typically on a 0.00–5.00 scale. Computed from player ratings and used for workshop ranking, featured content selection, and creator reputation scoring.
attributes.references: Gaming Internal Data Standards; GameAnalytics/Amplitude Player Behavior Analytics

attributes.name: removed_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the UGC submission was removed from public availability, either by the creator, platform moderation, or automated policy enforcement. Null if the submission has not been removed. Supports compliance audit trails.
attributes.references: Gaming Internal Data Standards; European Commission Digital Services Act; GDPR Article 17 (Right to Erasure); ISO/IEC 27001

attributes.name: report_count
attributes.description: Cumulative number of player-submitted reports flagging this UGC submission for policy violations (e.g., inappropriate content, IP infringement, spam). Triggers automated moderation escalation thresholds.
attributes.references: Gaming Internal Data Standards; European Commission Digital Services Act; FTC Consumer Protection Standards

attributes.name: requires_base_game_dlc
attributes.business_glossary_term: UGC Requires Base Game DLC Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this UGC submission requires the player to own a specific Downloadable Content (DLC) pack in addition to the base game in order to use the content. Used for entitlement validation and player-facing compatibility warnings.
attributes.references: Gaming Internal Data Standards; Steamworks SDK

attributes.name: submission_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the UGC submission within the moderation and publishing workflow. Controls visibility, download availability, and monetization eligibility. Serves as the LIFECYCLE_STATUS for this MASTER_RESOURCE. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: draft|pending_review|approved|rejected|removed|archived — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: Gaming Internal Data Standards; ESRB Content Guidelines; PEGI Content Guidelines

attributes.name: submission_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the UGC submission was first submitted by the creator for review. Represents the principal business event time for this entity. Used for SLA tracking of moderation turnaround and community activity trend analysis.

attributes.name: tags
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of community-defined tags applied to the UGC submission for discoverability and categorization (e.g., 'horror,multiplayer,competitive'). Used for search indexing and recommendation engine inputs.

attributes.name: title
attributes.description: Human-readable title of the UGC submission as provided by the creator. Used for display in community portals, workshop listings, and search indexing. Serves as the primary IDENTITY_LABEL for this MASTER_RESOURCE.

attributes.name: ugc_submission_description
attributes.description: Full text description of the UGC submission as authored by the creator. Describes the content, features, installation instructions, and intended use. Used for community discovery, search indexing, and moderation review.

attributes.name: ugc_type
attributes.description: Category of UGC asset submitted by the player. Drives content moderation workflows, monetization eligibility rules, and community portal routing. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: map|mod|skin|game_mode|guide|fan_art|other — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: Gaming Internal Data Standards; IGDA Community Standards

attributes.name: version_number
attributes.description: Semantic version number of the UGC submission (e.g., 1.0, 2.3.1). Tracks iterative updates by the creator and enables compatibility checks with game engine versions. Aligns with Perforce Helix Core versioning conventions.
attributes.references: Perforce Helix Core Version Control Standards; Semantic Versioning (semver.org)

SSOT for all guild and clan social structures.

attributes.name: guild_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for the guild or clan social group. Primary key for the guild master entity in the community domain.

Studios track which campaigns drive guild formation and activity for ROI measurement a

attributes.name: game_title_id

attributes.name: age_restricted
attributes.description: Indicates whether this guild enforces an age restriction on membership, requiring members to be 18+ or meet a minimum age threshold. Supports COPPA and GDPR compliance for minor protection.
attributes.references: COPPA (Children's Online Privacy Protection Act); GDPR Supervisory Authorities

attributes.name: banner_asset_ref
attributes.description: Reference path or URI to the guild's banner or header image asset stored in the digital asset management system. Displayed on the guild's community profile page.
attributes.references: Perforce Helix Core Digital Asset Management Standard

attributes.name: content_rating
attributes.description: Content maturity rating applicable to this guild's activities and communications, aligned with ESRB rating categories. Used to enforce age-appropriate community access controls.
attributes.references: ESRB (Entertainment Software Rating Board); PEGI (Pan European Game Information)

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: System timestamp recording when the guild record was first created in the data platform. Supports audit trail and data lineage requirements.

attributes.name: disbanded_date
attributes.description: Date on which the guild was officially disbanded or dissolved. Null for active guilds. Used for historical reporting and community lifecycle analytics.

attributes.name: discord_server_code
attributes.description: External Discord server identifier linked to this guild's community communication channel. Used for cross-platform community integration and player support routing.

attributes.name: emblem_asset_ref
attributes.description: Reference path or URI to the guild's emblem or badge image asset stored in the digital asset management system (Perforce Helix Core / CDN). Used for rendering the guild icon in-game and on community portals.
attributes.references: Perforce Helix Core Digital Asset Management Standard

attributes.name: external_website_url
attributes.description: URL of the guild's external website or community page, if maintained outside the game platform. Used for community discovery and marketing.

attributes.name: founded_date

attributes.name: guild_description
attributes.description: Free-text description of the guild written by the guild leader, outlining the guild's goals, rules, play style, and membership expectations. Displayed on the guild profile page.

attributes.name: guild_name
attributes.description: The full display name of the guild or clan as chosen by the founder and visible to all players in-game and on community platforms.

attributes.name: guild_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the guild. Active guilds are operational; disbanded guilds have been dissolved; suspended guilds are under moderation review; pending guilds are awaiting approval.

attributes.name: guild_type
attributes.description: Categorical classification of the guild's primary play style and purpose. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: casual|competitive|roleplay|social|esports|pve — promote to reference product if additional types are needed]

attributes.name: is_esports_org
attributes.description: Indicates whether this guild is formally affiliated with or operates as an esports organization participating in sanctioned leagues or tournaments.

attributes.name: is_verified
attributes.description: Indicates whether the guild has been officially verified by the platform or community team, typically for esports organizations or notable community groups. Verified guilds may receive special badges and visibility.

attributes.name: language_code
attributes.description: Primary language spoken within the guild, expressed as an IETF BCP 47 language tag (e.g., en, fr, de, zh-CN). Used for community matching and localization.

attributes.name: last_activity_date
attributes.description: Date of the most recent recorded activity within the guild (e.g., member login, guild event, chat message). Used to identify inactive or dormant guilds for lifecycle management.

attributes.name: member_capacity
attributes.description: Maximum number of players allowed to be members of this guild simultaneously, as configured by the guild leader or constrained by game design rules.

attributes.name: member_count
attributes.description: Current number of active members in the guild at the time of the last record update. Used for capacity management and community health reporting.

attributes.name: min_player_level
attributes.description: Minimum in-game player level required to apply for or join this guild. Used to enforce skill and progression gates for guild membership.

attributes.name: nps_score
attributes.description: Net Promoter Score (NPS) aggregated from member satisfaction surveys for this guild, ranging from -100 to 100. Used to measure community health and member loyalty within the guild.
attributes.references: Internal Community Health Analytics Standard; GameAnalytics/Amplitude

attributes.name: platform
attributes.description: Primary gaming platform on which the guild operates. Cross-platform guilds span multiple platforms. Used for platform-specific community analytics and matchmaking.

attributes.name: prestige_level
attributes.description: Current prestige or rank level of the guild derived from accumulated XP and achievements. Determines access to exclusive guild perks, rewards, and in-game content.

attributes.name: privacy_level
attributes.description: Visibility setting for the guild profile. Public guilds are discoverable by all players; private guilds are hidden from search; unlisted guilds are accessible only via direct link.
attributes.references: GDPR Supervisory Authorities; Internal Community Management Standard

attributes.name: pve_focus
attributes.description: Indicates whether the guild's primary activity focus is Player versus Environment (PvE) content such as raids, dungeons, and cooperative missions.

attributes.name: pvp_focus
attributes.description: Indicates whether the guild's primary activity focus is Player versus Player (PvP) content, as opposed to Player versus Environment (PvE) or social/roleplay activities.

attributes.name: recruitment_status
attributes.description: Current recruitment posture of the guild indicating whether new members may join freely (open), by invitation only (invite_only), via application (application), or not at all (closed).

attributes.name: source_system
attributes.description: Identifies the operational system of record from which this guild record originated (e.g., GameAnalytics, Amplitude, Salesforce CRM, or a custom in-house platform). Supports data lineage and reconciliation.

attributes.name: tag
attributes.description: Short alphanumeric abbreviation or clan tag (2–6 characters) displayed alongside player names in-game to identify guild membership (e.g., [APEX]).

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: System timestamp recording when the guild record was most recently modified in the data platform. Supports change tracking, audit trail, and incremental ETL processing.
attributes.references: ISO/IEC 27001 Information Security Management; GDPR Supervisory Authorities

attributes.name: weekly_active_members
attributes.description: Count of guild members who were active in-game during the most recent 7-day period. Key community health metric analogous to Weekly Active Users (WAU) at the guild level.

attributes.name: xp_total
attributes.description: Cumulative experience points (XP) earned by the guild through collective member activity, guild quests, and in-game events. Drives guild level progression and prestige rankings.

products.name: guild_membership

Records player reference, guild reference, membership role (leader/officer/member/recruit), join date, promotion history flag, contribution score, activity status, invite source, and departure date/reason when applicable. Manages the M:N relationship between players and guilds with full lifecycle data.

attributes.name: guild_membership_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for each guild membership record. Serves as the primary key for the guild_membership association entity, tracking the full lifecycle of a player's participation within a guild or clan.

attributes.name: consent_policy_id

attributes.description: Reference to the guild or clan that the player belongs to. Represents the guild-side of the M:N relationship between players and guilds.

attributes.name: moderation_action_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to community.moderation_action. Adding guild_membership.moderatio

attributes.name: player_account_id
attributes.description: Reference to the player who holds this guild membership. Represents the player-side of the M:N relationship between players and guilds.

attributes.name: activity_status
attributes.description: Derived classification of the member's recent engagement level within the guild context, based on login frequency and guild-specific interactions. Distinct from membership_status; used by guild leaders and community managers to identify at-risk members for retention outreach.

attributes.name: consent_timestamp
attributes.description: The precise date and time at which the player granted data processing consent for guild membership data. Required for GDPR audit trails. Null if consent has not been obtained or is not applicable.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 7 (Conditions for Consent); GDPR Supervisory Authorities

attributes.name: contribution_score
attributes.description: Numeric score representing the player's cumulative contributions to the guild, such as donated resources, completed guild quests, or participation in guild events. Used by guild leaders to assess member value and inform promotion or removal decisions.

attributes.name: csat_score
attributes.description: The most recent Customer Satisfaction Score (CSAT) rating provided by this player regarding their guild experience, typically on a 1–5 scale. Complements NPS for community health measurement and player care operations.
attributes.references: Zendesk Player Support; Internal CSAT Tracking

attributes.name: current_role_since_date
attributes.description: The date on which the player was assigned their current membership_role. Enables tenure-in-role calculations and supports promotion eligibility logic distinct from overall guild tenure.

attributes.name: data_processing_consent
attributes.description: Indicates whether the player has provided explicit consent for processing of their guild membership and community interaction data. Required for GDPR compliance for players in EU jurisdictions. True when valid consent is on record.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 6 (Lawful Basis for Processing); GDPR Supervisory Authorities

attributes.name: departure_date
attributes.description: The calendar date on which the player left or was removed from the guild. Null when the membership is still active. Used for churn analysis and guild stability reporting.

attributes.name: departure_reason
attributes.description: Categorical reason explaining why the player's membership ended. Supports community health analysis and guild churn root-cause reporting. Null when membership is still active.

attributes.name: guild_chat_messages_sent
attributes.description: Cumulative count of messages sent by the player in the guild chat channel since joining. A key social engagement indicator used by community managers to assess member communication activity and guild cohesion.

attributes.name: guild_events_participated
attributes.description: Cumulative count of guild-organized events (raids, tournaments, guild quests, PvP battles) in which the player has participated since joining. Used to measure event engagement and identify high-value community contributors.

attributes.name: has_promotion_history
attributes.description: Indicates whether the player has ever been promoted to a higher role within this guild. True when at least one role promotion event exists in the membership history. Used as a quick filter for identifying experienced, trusted members.

attributes.name: invite_source
attributes.description: The channel or mechanism through which the player was recruited into the guild. Supports K-Factor viral coefficient analysis and community growth attribution. attributes.references: AppsFlyer/Adjust Mobile Attribution and Marketing Analytics

attributes.name: is_age_verified

attributes.name: is_founder
attributes.description: Indicates whether this player was one of the founding members who created the guild. Founders may retain special privileges or recognition even if their current role has changed. Used for community heritage and loyalty analytics.

attributes.name: join_date
attributes.description: The calendar date on which the player officially joined the guild. Used for tenure calculations, retention analysis, and D1/D7/D30 guild engagement cohort reporting.

attributes.name: join_timestamp
attributes.description: Precise date and time at which the player's guild membership was activated. Provides sub-day precision for event sequencing, funnel analysis, and audit trails beyond what join_date alone provides.

attributes.name: last_active_date
attributes.description: The most recent calendar date on which the player performed any guild-related activity. Used to identify dormant members, trigger re-engagement campaigns, and support inactivity-based removal workflows.

attributes.name: membership_role
attributes.description: The functional role held by the player within the guild hierarchy. Determines permissions, responsibilities, and visibility within guild operations. attributes.name: membership_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the player's guild membership. attributes.name: membership_tier
attributes.description: Prestige or progression tier assigned to the player's membership within the guild, reflecting cumulative achievement and standing. Used for tiered reward distribution, exclusive content access, and community recognition programs.

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for guild officers or community managers to record contextual notes about the membership, such as reasons for role changes, special circumstances, or moderation observations. Not displayed to the member.

attributes.name: nps_score

attributes.name: platform_code

attributes.name: previous_role
attributes.description: The membership role held by the player immediately before their current role assignment. Provides a single-step promotion/demotion audit trail without requiring a full history table query for the most recent transition.

attributes.name: pvp_wins_for_guild

attributes.description: Cumulative count of PvP (Player versus Player) match victories the player has contributed to guild-ranked competitions since joining. Used to assess competitive contribution and inform officer promotion decisions.

attributes.name: record_updated_timestamp

attributes.description: Identifies the operational system of record from which this guild membership record originated or was last updated. Supports data lineage tracking in the Databricks Silver Layer and ETL audit processes.

attributes.name: weekly_active_days
attributes.description: Number of distinct days in the most recently completed calendar week on which the player was active within the guild context (e.g., participated in guild chat, guild quests, or guild events). attributes.name: closed_at
attributes.description: Timestamp when the ticket was permanently closed by the system (typically 72 hours after solved status). A closed ticket cannot be reopened. Distinct from solved_at — represents the final end-of-lifecycle event.

attributes.name: comment_count

attributes.name: created_at
attributes.description: Timestamp when this support ticket record was first ingested into the Gaming lakehouse Silver layer. Maps to RECORD_AUDIT_CREATED category for TRANSACTION_HEADER role. Distinct from opened_at which reflects the Zendesk event time.
attributes.references: Databricks Lakehouse Silver Layer Ingestion Standard

attributes.name: csat_comment
attributes.description: Free-text feedback provided by the player alongside their CSAT rating. Used for qualitative analysis, NPS correlation, and identifying systemic support issues. Classified confidential as it may contain player sentiment and operational details.
attributes.references: Zendesk CSAT Survey — comment field; GDPR Article 5

attributes.name: csat_score
attributes.description: Player-submitted Customer Satisfaction (CSAT) rating for this ticket, typically on a 1–5 scale collected via post-resolution survey. Null if the player did not respond to the survey. Core metric for player care quality and agent performance evaluation.
attributes.references: Zendesk CSAT Survey; IGDA Player Experience Standards

attributes.name: due_at
attributes.description: The SLA deadline timestamp by which this ticket must be resolved to avoid an SLA breach. Set automatically based on ticket priority and channel SLA policy at time of creation. Used for real-time SLA monitoring and proactive escalation triggers.
attributes.references: Zendesk Ticket Object — due_at field; Internal SLA Policy

attributes.name: escalation_tier
attributes.description: Numeric tier indicating the escalation level of the ticket. Tier 1 = frontline agent; Tier 2 = senior specialist; Tier 3 = engineering/trust-and-safety; Tier 4 = executive escalation. Increments when a ticket is escalated due to complexity, SLA breach, or player demand.
attributes.references: Zendesk Ticket custom field — escalation_tier; Internal Escalation Policy

attributes.name: first_response_at
attributes.description: Timestamp of the first public agent reply on this ticket. Used alongside opened_at to derive first_response_time_seconds and to validate SLA compliance at the event level. Distinct from first_response_time_seconds which is the computed duration.
attributes.references: Zendesk SLA Metric — first_reply_time event timestamp

attributes.name: first_response_time_seconds
attributes.description: Elapsed time in seconds between ticket creation and the first public agent reply. Core SLA metric for player support operations. Used to calculate SLA compliance rates and benchmark channel performance. Maps to QUANTITATIVE_RESULT for non-monetary transaction.
attributes.references: Zendesk SLA Metric — reply_time; IGDA Support KPI Framework

attributes.name: game_version
attributes.description: The version string of the game client the player was running when the issue occurred. Used to correlate support spikes with specific build releases, hotfixes, or DLC deployments. Aligns with Perforce Helix Core build labels.
attributes.references: Zendesk Ticket custom field — game_version; Perforce Helix Core Build Label Convention

attributes.name: gdpr_data_request_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this ticket contains or is associated with a GDPR data subject request (e.g., right of access, right to erasure, right to portability). Triggers mandatory compliance workflows with statutory response deadlines under GDPR Article 12.
attributes.references: GDPR Articles 12–22 (Data Subject Rights); GDPR Supervisory Authorities

attributes.name: group_name

attributes.name: is_first_contact_resolved
attributes.description: Indicates whether the player's issue was fully resolved in a single interaction without requiring escalation, follow-up, or reopening. First Contact Resolution (FCR) is a primary KPI for support efficiency and player satisfaction.
attributes.references: IGDA Support KPI Framework — FCR metric

attributes.name: issue_category
attributes.description: Top-level classification of the player's support issue. Drives routing rules, SLA assignment, and reporting dashboards. 'billing' covers IAP/MTX disputes; 'technical' covers FPS drops, crashes, connectivity; 'account' covers login, bans, data requests; 'gameplay' covers bugs, exploits, NPC behavior; 'harassment' covers PvP/community conduct violations.
attributes.references: Zendesk Ticket custom field — issue_type; ESRB Community Standards; GDPR Article 17 (erasure requests under account category)

attributes.name: issue_subcategory
attributes.description: Second-level classification providing granular issue detail within the parent issue_category. Examples: under 'billing' — refund_request, duplicate_charge, iap_not_received; under 'technical' — crash_on_launch, matchmaking_failure, save_data_corruption. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: refund_request|duplicate_charge|iap_not_received|crash_on_launch|matchmaking_failure|save_data_corruption|account_ban|login_failure|data_deletion_request|harassment_report|exploit_report|other — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: Zendesk Ticket custom field — issue_subtype; Internal Support Taxonomy

attributes.name: last_assignee_update_at
attributes.description: Timestamp of the most recent comment or update submitted by the assigned agent on this ticket. Used to monitor agent responsiveness and identify tickets that have gone stale on the agent side.

attributes.name: last_requester_update_at
attributes.description: Timestamp of the most recent comment or update submitted by the player (requester) on this ticket. Used to identify stale tickets awaiting player response and to trigger automated follow-up reminders.

attributes.name: locale
attributes.description: BCP 47 locale code representing the player's language and region at time of ticket submission (e.g., 'en-US', 'fr-FR', 'ja-JP'). Used for routing to language-appropriate agents, localization of automated responses, and regional support volume analysis.
attributes.references: Zendesk Ticket Object — locale field; BCP 47 Language Tag Standard; GDPR Article 12 (communication in intelligible language)

attributes.name: opened_at

attributes.name: organization_code

attributes.name: player_account_type
attributes.description: Classification of the player's monetization tier at the time of ticket submission. F2P (Free-to-Play) players, premium purchasers, subscribers, and high-spending 'whale' players may receive differentiated SLA treatment. Supports priority routing and ARPPU-aware support strategies.
attributes.references: Zendesk Ticket custom field — player_segment; Internal Player Segmentation Model

attributes.name: reopen_count
attributes.description: Number of times this ticket has been reopened after being marked as solved. A high reopen count indicates unresolved issues, poor first-contact resolution, or player dissatisfaction. Used in quality assurance and agent coaching workflows.

attributes.name: resolution_time_seconds
attributes.description: Total elapsed time in seconds from ticket creation to the ticket being marked as solved. Key operational metric for support efficiency, SLA compliance, and player satisfaction correlation analysis.
attributes.references: Zendesk SLA Metric — resolution_time; IGDA Support KPI Framework

attributes.name: satisfaction_rating
attributes.description: Zendesk satisfaction rating state indicating whether a CSAT survey was offered, responded to, and the outcome. Distinct from the numeric csat_score — this field captures the survey delivery and response state.

attributes.name: sla_breach_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this ticket breached its assigned Service Level Agreement (SLA) target for first response or resolution time. True = SLA was breached. Used for operational KPI reporting, agent performance reviews, and SLA compliance dashboards.
attributes.references: Zendesk SLA Policy Object; IGDA Support Operations Standards

attributes.name: solved_at

attributes.description: Priority level assigned to the ticket, determining SLA tier and queue routing. 'urgent' is reserved for critical issues such as account compromise, payment fraud, or widespread outages affecting CCU.

'new' = unassigned; 'open' = assigned and active; 'pending' = awaiting player response; 'on_hold' = awaiting third-party; 'solved' = agent-resolved; 'closed' = system-locked after solve.

attributes.name: updated_at

attributes.name: content_format

When true, the article may be restricted from display to players under the applicable age threshold.

attributes.name: gdpr_data_flag

attributes.description: Indicates whether this article references player personal data handling procedures (e.g., data deletion requests, account privacy settings). When true, the article is subject to GDPR supervisory authority review and must align with current privacy policy.

attributes.name: last_updated_at

attributes.description: The real-world date and time when the alleged violation occurred, as reported by the submitting player or inferred from game session logs. Distinct from the report submission timestamp.
attributes.references: GameAnalytics/Amplitude Event Timestamp; Internal Community Policy

attributes.name: is_automated_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this report was generated by an automated detection system (e.g., anti-cheat engine, chat filter, UGC scanner) rather than a player submission. Distinguishes system-generated from player-generated reports.
attributes.references: Internal Anti-Cheat Policy; GameAnalytics/Amplitude Event Detection

attributes.name: is_minor_involved
attributes.description: Indicates whether the reporting or reported player is identified as a minor (under 13 or under 18 depending on jurisdiction). Triggers COPPA-compliant handling procedures and elevated moderation priority.
attributes.references: COPPA; GDPR Article 8; ESRB; PEGI; Internal Child Safety Policy

attributes.name: is_repeat_report
attributes.description: Indicates whether the reporting player has previously submitted a report against the same reported entity. True signals potential targeted harassment by the reporter or a persistent offender pattern.
attributes.references: Internal Community Policy; FTC Consumer Protection

attributes.name: moderation_queue
attributes.description: The moderation queue to which this report was routed based on violation severity, reporter history, and automated triage rules. Determines handling SLA tier.
attributes.references: Zendesk Queue Management; Internal Community Policy

attributes.name: report_description
attributes.description: Free-text narrative provided by the reporting player describing the alleged violation in their own words. Primary evidence input for moderator review.
attributes.references: Zendesk Ticket Description; Internal Community Policy

attributes.name: report_number
attributes.description: Human-readable, externally referenceable business identifier for the report (e.g., RPT-0000123456). Used in player communications, Zendesk tickets, and audit trails.
attributes.references: Zendesk Ticket Reference; Internal Community Policy

attributes.name: report_source_channel
attributes.description: The channel through which the report was submitted (e.g., in-game report UI, web portal, mobile app, Zendesk support form). Informs channel-specific moderation workflow routing.
attributes.references: Zendesk Channel Tracking; Internal Community Policy

attributes.name: report_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the player report within the moderation workflow. Drives queue management and SLA tracking. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: pending|under_review|actioned|dismissed|escalated|closed — promote to reference product if additional statuses are required]
attributes.references: Zendesk Ticket Status; Internal Community Moderation Policy

attributes.name: reported_entity_prior_violation_count
attributes.description: Number of confirmed prior violations on the reported entity's record at the time of this report. Informs severity escalation and repeat-offender enforcement policies.
attributes.references: Internal Community Enforcement Policy; ESRB; PEGI

attributes.name: reported_entity_reference
attributes.description: Identifier of the entity being reported (player, post, UGC item, or chat message). The entity type is specified in reported_entity_type.

attributes.name: reported_entity_type
attributes.description: Discriminator indicating the type of entity being reported. Determines which downstream moderation workflow and evidence schema applies. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: player|post|ugc|chat|clan|profile — promote to reference product if additional types are required]
attributes.references: Internal Community Policy; IGDA Community Standards

attributes.name: reporter_account_age_days
attributes.description: Age of the reporting player's account in days at the time of report submission. Used in automated triage to weight report credibility and detect smurf or throwaway accounts.

attributes.name: reporter_prior_report_count
attributes.description: Total number of reports previously submitted by the reporting player at the time of this submission. Supports reporter credibility scoring and abuse-of-report-system detection.

attributes.name: resolution_action
attributes.description: The specific enforcement action taken as a result of this report. Drives enforcement analytics and appeals tracking. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: warning_issued|account_suspended|account_banned|content_removed|no_action|escalated_to_trust_safety — promote to reference product if additional actions are required]
attributes.references: ESRB; PEGI; FTC; European Commission Digital Services Act; Internal Community Enforcement Policy

attributes.name: resolution_notes
attributes.description: Moderator-authored free-text notes documenting the rationale for the resolution decision, evidence reviewed, and any mitigating factors considered. Critical for appeals and audit trails.
attributes.references: Zendesk Internal Notes; Internal Community Policy; GDPR Article 5

attributes.name: resolution_time_hours
attributes.description: Actual elapsed time in hours from report submission to resolution. Calculated field stored for operational reporting; used to assess moderation efficiency and SLA adherence.
attributes.references: Internal SLA Policy; Zendesk Resolution Metrics

attributes.name: resolved_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the report was fully resolved (actioned or dismissed). Used to calculate end-to-end resolution time and SLA compliance.
attributes.references: Zendesk Resolution Time; Internal SLA Policy; GDPR Article 12 (response timelines)

attributes.name: reviewed_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when a moderator first opened and began reviewing this report. Used to calculate time-to-first-review SLA metrics.
attributes.references: Zendesk First Response Time; Internal SLA Policy

attributes.name: severity_level
attributes.description: Assessed severity of the reported violation, assigned by automated triage or moderator review. Drives prioritization within the moderation queue and escalation thresholds.
attributes.references: Internal Community Policy; ESRB; PEGI; European Commission Digital Services Act

attributes.name: sla_target_hours
attributes.description: The target resolution time in hours for this report based on its severity level and moderation queue tier. Used to measure SLA compliance and moderator performance.
attributes.references: Internal SLA Policy; European Commission Digital Services Act

attributes.name: submitted_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the reporting player formally submitted this report to the moderation system. Used as the BUSINESS_EVENT_TIMESTAMP for SLA measurement and queue aging.
attributes.references: Zendesk Ticket Created At; GDPR Article 5; Internal SLA Policy

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this player_report record was last modified in the data platform. Tracks moderator actions, status transitions, and resolution updates for audit compliance.
attributes.references: ISO/IEC 27001; GDPR Article 5; Internal Data Governance Policy

attributes.name: violation_category
attributes.description: Primary classification of the alleged violation (e.g., harassment, cheating, hate_speech, spam, inappropriate_ugc, account_sharing, exploiting). Drives routing to specialized moderation queues. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: harassment|cheating|hate_speech|spam|inappropriate_ugc|account_sharing|exploiting|other — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: ESRB Content Guidelines; PEGI Code of Conduct; FTC Consumer Protection; Internal Community Policy

attributes.name: violation_subcategory
attributes.description: Secondary classification providing granular detail within the violation category (e.g., within harassment: verbal_abuse, sexual_harassment, doxxing). Enables fine-grained moderation analytics and policy tuning.
attributes.references: ESRB Content Guidelines; PEGI Code of Conduct; Internal Community Policy

Tracks event name, event type, associated game title, organizer reference, start/end dates, participation eligibility, prize/reward description, registration count, participant count, platform, and event status (upcoming/active/completed/cancelled).

attributes.name: influencer_id

attributes.name: jurisdiction_id

attributes.name: live_ops_cycle_id

attributes.description: Foreign key linking to licensing.mtx_catalog. Business justification: Events promote specific MTX items (e.g., holiday skins, event bundles). Linking events to catalog items enables targeted marketing, event-specific discounts, and tracks promotional SKU performance.

attributes.name: network_region_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to infrastructure.network_region. Business justification: Events often region-locked or region-specific (tournaments, beta tests). Required for eligibility enforcement, capacity planning, and ensuring infrastructure readiness for regional event load.

attributes.name: organizer_player_account_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to player.player_account. Business justification: Community events can be player-organized (guild tournaments, fan events). The organizer_player_account_id FK identifies the responsible player for moderation accountability, prize distribution, and co

attributes.name: parent_event_community_event_id
attributes.description: Self-referencing identifier linking this event to its parent event in a series or campaign hierarchy (e.g., a weekly challenge belonging to a seasonal campaign). Null for top-level events.

attributes.name: parent_seasonal_event_id
